---
name: optimise
description: Read the digest of the records of the features merged and not yet analysed, rank the root causes of their failures, and make the smallest change to the overlay that removes each major one. A cause only an engine change fixes becomes a drafted issue, never filed.
disable-model-invocation: true
---

<!-- Generated by Bernard the taktician. Do not edit: change .factory/ and run `bernard sync`. -->

The `digest` step ran `bernard optimise digest`: its `handoff.json`, in the record of the segment's previous step, lists the features to analyse (`features`) and the causes found in their records: failed attempts by failure class, crashes, steps that exhausted their failures, and the feedback of human reviews, each cause dated by its last occurrence (`lastAt`) and holding at most 3 `samples` of its evidence, the latest first. A sample names its feature, ticket and attempt, the `record` that holds it whole, the attempt's `handoff.json` or the log line as `path:line`, and an `excerpt` of it: the error of a failed attempt, with the first blocking and major findings of its handoff cut short, the error of a crash, or the feedback of a change request. The digest also holds `steps`, the profile of each step across those features, ranked by `totalMs`: its `attempts`, `firstPassRate`, `medianMs`, `p90Ms`, `totalMs`, `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `costUsd` when known, the `models` and `efforts` it ran with, and `withoutUsage`, the attempts whose record holds no usage. Read it, and never read the remote again: the list of features is fixed.

No feature to analyse: change nothing and end `passed`, with a summary that says so.

1. Find the root cause behind each cause of the digest, not its symptom. Start from the excerpts of its samples, and read the file a sample's `record` names only when its excerpt leaves the root cause open: each file read stays in this session's context; then the skill, slot or config of `.factory/` the step ran with. Then check it is still live: the records span weeks while the overlay and the engine kept changing. Its `lastAt` is the date of its last occurrence; `git log --since <lastAt> -- .factory/` and the history of the rendered files list what changed after it, an engine upgrade included. A cause one of those changes fixed is recorded with the action `none` and no `rank`, its `change` naming the commit, and never fixed again.
2. Rank the live causes by cost: the lost attempts first (`failure`), then the crashes (`crash`), then the human rounds (`changes-requested`), and within each kind the highest `count` first. A cause's cost is its `count`: each occurrence is one attempt, crash or round lost. An `exhausted` cause costs nothing of its own, since the `failure` causes of its step already count its attempts: it tells which failures parked a ticket. Walk the ranking and add up the costs: the causes it takes to reach about 80% of the cost of all the live causes are the major ones, the others are minor. State each cause's `cost` as the records give it: its attempts, crashes or rounds lost, in how many features. This ranking is the failures lens: its causes are recorded with `lens` `failures`.
3. Challenge the usage the same way, as the usage lens: rank the `steps` by `totalMs`, never by `costUsd`, a sum that counts only the attempts reporting a cost, and walk the ranking: the steps it takes to reach about 80% of the total are the major ones, the others are minor. Read `withoutUsage` as a caveat: a step whose attempts mostly lack usage is not challenged on its time, and say so in the cause. The levers are `models` (the model of a tier) in `.factory/factory.config.ts`, and a step's `model` and a step's `effort` in `.factory/pipelines.ts`. Two rules: a step that passes first time (`firstPassRate` high) and is slow or costly gets a cheaper model or a lower effort; a step that keeps failing on a cheap model or a low effort, by the failures lens, gets a stronger one. The quality risk of a cheaper model or a lower effort is the `tradeoff` of the cause. A cause of this lens is recorded with `lens` `usage`, its `cost` in minutes or dollars, and it names the step and the figures of its profile.
4. Act on each major cause, in the order of the ranking, with the smallest change to `.factory/` that removes it: a line in a slot or a skill override, a scope, a script, a handoff field. Make at most 3 changes to the overlay in a run, both lenses together, to bound the churn a human reviews: a major cause past the third is recorded with the action `none`, its `change` saying it was left for a later run, and comes back when the next features' records show it again. Act on one minor cause only when no cause is major. Make the value and the price of each change or draft explicit: its `tradeoff` is what it costs, the context it adds to the sessions of each step that reads it (a slot many steps read costs in every one of their sessions), the steps or tickets it adds, and the risk it takes; its `expectedGain` what should drop; its `watch` what the next digest shows if it worked, such as the cause's `lastAt` staying before the change merged.
5. Touch nothing outside `.factory/` and the feature folders: never `core/`, the engine or the code of the project.
6. A cause that only an engine change fixes is drafted, not filed: a headless step does not publish outward-facing content. Search the issues of the engine's repository first, the `repository` of the engine's `package.json`, open and closed. An open issue that covers the cause gets an addition to its description, never a comment: trackers and agents read an issue's description, not its comments. The addition carries the new evidence: the features, the counts, the dates and the samples. A closed issue the cause extends gets a new issue that links it. With no such issue, or no access to that repository, draft a new issue. Write the draft in `optimise.json`, with the action `issue`, and the human files it from the pull request.
7. Write `docs/features/<feature>/optimise.json` in each analysed feature: `{ analysedAt, causes: [{ lens, id, step, failureClass?, summary, rank?, action, cost, change, tradeoff?, expectedGain?, watch?, files?, issue? }] }`, with `analysedAt` an ISO 8601 date and time, `summary` the root cause, the other fields as in your handoff, and `issue` as `{ title, body }` for a new issue or `{ number, addition }` for an addition to the description of the open issue `number`. The causes of the file are the ones that touch the feature. A cause seen and not acted on is `none`: the file records that it was seen. A feature with a file is analysed: the next digest leaves it out.
8. When you changed a file, run the checks until they are green:

`npm --prefix modern run check`, which runs Biome (formatter, linter, import order), the type-checker (`tsc --noEmit`) and the unit tests (Vitest, `modern/src/**/*.test.ts`).

Your handoff is `{ summary, causes }`: one entry per cause of the digest, in the order of the ranking, with the fields of its `optimise.json` entry but `step`, `failureClass` and `summary`, and its `issue` as `{ title, number? }`. The `pull-request` step builds the pull request's table of the causes from it.
